title: Profiling-guided microbatch & state-cache advisor with synthetic anchor corpus and safe-apply playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Build an end-to-end advisor that recommends microbatch sizing and state-cache (KV) eligibility per model/profile, validates recommendations against a synthetic anchor corpus, and provides a procedurally-guarded safe-apply + rollback playbook for automated and manual rollouts. This ticket covers: (1) a profiling pipeline to produce workload fingerprints (token length distribution, prefix reuse, kv-hit-rate estimate), (2) an optimizer that maps fingerprints -> candidate configs (microbatch, max_batch_latency, kv_policy), (3) a synthetic anchor corpus generator to approximate customer prompts for black-box regressions, (4) an acceptance harness with statistical tests and counterexample sampling, and (5) a stepwise apply/rollback orchestration with human gates and monitoring hooks.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Aisha Khan: Created initial ticket after spike with runtime team. Spike showed 12-18% token-cost reduction on a stable prefix-reuse workload using 4-8 microbatch with aggressive KV retention. Noted potential regression on long-context completion fidelity.

2026-02-28 - Miguel Ortega: Added profiling prototype (link in artifacts). Profiling extracts: mean request tokens, 90th percentile prefix overlap, per-call kv-cache hit probability estimate, and latency tail. Prototype runs on a 24h production trace sample (anonymized) and outputs fingerprint vectors.

2026-03-03 - Priya Shah (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. We need: false-negative rate < 2% for quality regressions over anchor corpus, and auto-rollback TTL <= 10 minutes for P99 latency spikes. Also asked for product UX hooks: a console preview of expected cost delta and sample regenerated outputs for human review.

2026-03-05 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented synthetic anchor corpus generator. Approach: cluster trace by fingerprint, then synthesize prompts by re-stitching anonymized prefix templates and diversify completions via temperature sweeps. Added option to inject human-written edge-case prompts from survey corpus.

2026-03-08 - Design feedback (Liam Park): Asked that the console show representative diffs with token-level alignment and highlight hallucination-like changes. Suggested small embedded viewer for side-by-side outputs and a ‘confidence delta’ metric derived from log-prob delta across tokens.

2026-03-10 - Engineering note: Acceptance harness now runs three statistical checks: (a) token-level distribution shift (KS test) on top-k tokens, (b) semantic similarity on completions using reference embeddings with a soft threshold, and (c) a behavioral fingerprint delta that compares beam-span alignment. Preliminary thresholds tuned on holdout clusters.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Ortega: Opened draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4789. PR contains profiler, clusterer, and a candidate mapping table. Pending: integration tests with canary infra and console preview endpoints.

2026-03-13 - Security review request by Aisha Khan: Will the synthetic generator introduce PII? We plan to enforce strict anonymization and use synthetic-only substitution rules. Marking security_review_required=true in metadata.

2026-03-14 - QA update (Elena Novak): Set up A/B canary harness: staged rollout accepts candidate config only if (1) semantic-similarity mean >= 0.92 and (2) no single prompt exhibits >15% token-delta with decreased log-prob across the completion. Otherwise triggers automated hold and creates ENG sub-issue for manual audit.
Follow-ups: schedule a 30-minute demo with Console PM to review UX hooks (requested 2026-03-17).
